summary: Two processes on one SQLite file: no busy_timeout, deferred transactions, and caches that never hear each other
detail: From the v0.5.0 review (TODO #8, Reported). Nothing sets PRAGMA busy_timeout, and writes use db.transaction() (deferred; .immediate() is the fix), so the first write after another process's read lock fails SQLITE_BUSY at once and a valid write 500s. And the in-memory document cache is per process with no invalidation, so two server processes on one file serve divergent state. Either document one process per file as a hard rule (the skill's feature table now says 'one per file') or give SQLite a change channel like the Postgres listener. Repro: two `bun` processes calling registerDocs on the same file, one holding a read transaction while the other writes.
note: 2026-09-24: carried from TODO.md #8; still open after round 2.

summary: An included collection with no parent is filtered by the root's scope, and its rows fan out to every document of the prefix
detail: From the v0.5.0 review (TODO #9, Reported). loadCollection builds `WHERE <root scope columns> = ?` against the unparented collection's own table (with the default scope, `WHERE id = <docId>`: at most one row), and rowInScope returns true for any unparented collection, so a write to it reaches every open document of that prefix. In a tenant-scoped schema with a shared unparented collection that is a cross-document read. Needs a decision on what an unparented include means (load it all, as Postgres list-mode include does, or refuse it in defineDoc). No test covers the shape.
note: 2026-09-24: carried from TODO.md #9; needs a decision.

summary: A whole-row replace means two things: the JSON file replaces the row, SQLite and Postgres merge the fields sent
detail: From the second review pass (TODO A3). `replace /coll/id` with a partial value drops the missing fields on the JSON-file backend (RFC 6902) and merges them on SQLite and Postgres. The skill's 'Backends side by side' table now says so ('send it whole'). Either registerDoc merges at depth 2 to match, or the SQL backends replace. Repro: scratchpad/delta-reviewer/parity.ts, case 'whole-row replace with partial value'.
note: 2026-09-24: carried from TODO.md A3; documented, not unified.

summary: applyOps is RFC 6901 now but not RFC 6902: add at an array index overwrites, and replace/remove of a missing member do not fail
detail: Round 2 made the pointer grammar strict (leading /, escaping, a segment a string unless its parent is an array, no holes) and batches atomic. Two RFC 6902 rules are still delta's own: `add /arr/1` assigns instead of inserting (pinned by tests/core.test.ts 'add at array index OVERWRITES', documented in core.ts), and `replace`/`remove` of a member that is not there sets it / does nothing instead of failing (so the JSON file acks `remove /messages/nope` where SQLite answers 404). eta keeps its own src/json-patch.ts because it relies on insert (examples/ticker watchlist undo). Making delta's applyOps full RFC 6902 would let eta drop its copy; it changes documented behaviour, so it is Pete's call. Note the client applies broadcasts with the same applyOps, so a strict remove must not break fan-out of a row a client never had.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal; for Pete.

summary: The server handles a socket's messages concurrently, so a signed-in client that doesn't use onConnect still races its own authenticate
detail: Round 2 fixed the reconnect freeze on the client (connectWs(url, { onConnect }) runs before any doc (re)opens). Without the hook, two things remain: (1) createWs's message handler is async and not serialised per socket, so an `open` sent right after `authenticate` can be handled first and 401 (the 'variant B' of scratchpad/delta-reviewer/reconnect-auth.ts, re-run as scratchpad/round2-delta-fixer/reconnect-auth.ts); (2) a doc whose re-open got a 401 is only logged, never retried after a later authenticate. Per-socket serialisation would block slow handlers (recompute, registerMethod), so make it opt-in if it is done.
note: 2026-09-24: the server half of D2; client half fixed in round 2.

summary: SQLite has no auth: no gate, no owns, every socket may open every document of a prefix
detail: D9 from round 1. registerDocs takes no DeltaAuth, and open/delta never ask who is writing, so the SQLite tier cannot be multi-user safe without hand-written ws.on shims. The skill now says 'no auth' in the feature table and the SQLite quick start. A minimal fit with round 2's Postgres design: registerDocs(..., { auth, owns }) with the same default-deny as docTypeFromDef.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal; documented, not built.

summary: SQLite documents have no list mode, and a root row can only be made over the wire by an implied document
detail: D9 / dogfood A3, A4, P5. `defineDoc('todos:', { root: 'todos' })` opened as `todos:` looks for the row id '' and answers 404 (the message now says why). The shape of a document therefore differs from Postgres ({todos} there, {lists, todos} here). implied: true covers creating the root on first write; seeding with SQL covers the rest. Postgres also needs a raw INSERT for a single-mode root row.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal; the 404 names the rule now.

summary: SQLite opens and broadcasts carry valid_from and valid_to; Postgres strips them
detail: Seen while writing the SQLite quick start (scratchpad/round2-delta-fixer/sqlite-quickstart.ts): the open snapshot's rows and every echo include the temporal storage columns, which then sit in the client's doc.data. Postgres runs _delta_strip_temporal on both. inverseOf already strips them (withoutStorage). Stripping them on SQLite too would make the document shape the same on both SQL backends.
note: 2026-09-24: found in round 2; not fixed.

summary: Two validateOps: SQLite's (types, root fields) and Postgres's (a subset, which the listener never calls)
detail: CLAUDE.md used to say validateOps lived in src/schema.ts, shared; it does not. sqlite.ts has the full one; postgres/schema.ts exports a smaller one for callers, and the Postgres listener relies on delta_apply's checks instead (round 2 added unknown and required fields there). One shared validator is the DRY answer, but Postgres list-mode documents address rows on the root collection where SQLite treats /<root>/<x> as a root field, so it needs the document's mode.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal.

summary: doc.data is typed as a writable Signal, so an optimistic doc.data.set() type-checks
detail: Round 1 (delta.md §4). The skill's first rule is 'never optimistically update', but Doc<T>.data is ReturnType<typeof signal<T|null>>, so .set() and .patch() compile. Exposing ReadonlySignal<T|null> would make the rule a type error. It is a type-level breaking change for anyone who calls set() today.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal.

summary: The CLI is not agent-safe yet: no in-band token, watch never exits, delta answers only {ack}
detail: Round 1 (delta.md §4, §5). An auth-enabled server can't be reached (the token must not go in the URL, so it needs an in-band `call authenticate` first: --token / DELTA_TOKEN); `watch` never exits, so a Bash tool call hangs (--count N, --for 5s); `delta` returns only {ack}, not the ops as applied (--print-ops); and there is no offline `validate` or server `describe`. These come before an MCP wrapper.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal.

summary: CI installs the latest Bun unpinned, and /publish gates on bun run ci, which needs Docker
detail: ci.yml has `bun-version: latest` and publish.yml no version, so a Bun release can turn the gate red with no change here (round 1 saw exactly that on 1.4.2; the teardown was fixed upstream in 0.6.0). /publish runs `bun run ci` (Docker compose), which cannot run in the Claude Code web sandbox; CLAUDE.md gives the container gate instead. The release text is shared with railroad and eta.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal; release tooling is Pete's.

summary: examples/todos-vs-rls writes with raw INSERT/UPDATE, which the skill forbids
detail: Round 1 D11. delta.ts:120-139 writes the table directly, so nothing NOTIFYs; the example is never live, and its shared `todos:me` name is the D1 shape (with auth it now needs owns). Rewrite it on docTypeFromDef with owns, or drop it.
note: 2026-09-24: carried from round 1; examples are not in the package.

summary: A memory document's add /coll/- stores the key "-"; the JSON file and SQLite mint an id
detail: Round 2 made `add /<coll>/-` on a collection of rows mint an id on the JSON file (server.ts mintIds) and SQLite. registerMemory applies ops with applyOps directly, so `/people/-` on an object makes the key '-'. Memory documents are written by the server, so it bites less; mintIds could move to core for both.
note: 2026-09-24: found in round 2; not fixed.

summary: The test surface is not shared: mockClient and sendAndAwait are not in the package, and the pointer vectors are one test file's, not data eta can run
detail: Consumers can't import mockClient/sendAndAwait (tests/ is not in the package; the skill now says so). And the one pointer grammar is pinned by VECTORS in tests/postgres-pointer.test.ts, run through splitPath and _delta_split_path; as a JSON fixture (wire-vectors.json) eta's json-pointer.ts could run the same cases without a dependency (proposal-final.md §4). The team's larger idea is backend conformance stories (who does what, who sees it) run against JSON, SQLite and Postgres; tests/create-row.test.ts and tests/error-codes.test.ts are the first two.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal.

summary: On a temporal table, an explicit id the sequence later mints, or two adds of one id at once, make two live rows
detail: The 409 on an add of a live id (5bbff72) is an EXISTS check before the INSERT, and a temporal table's key is (id, valid_from), so nothing in the database stops a second live version. (1) `add /tnotes/1` then `add /tnotes/-`: nextval mints 1, the `-` branch skips the check, and the table holds two live rows with id 1 while `open` shows one (the first is lost). (2) Two adds of one explicit id through two documents (different doc locks) both pass the EXISTS check. Repro: scratchpad/round2-delta-reviewer-2/pg-temporal-id.test.ts (DELTA_TEST_PG_URL at a scratch database). Candidates: a partial unique index `(id) WHERE valid_to IS NULL` from codegen (a migration for existing tables), or setval past an explicit id, or refuse explicit ids other than undo's re-add.
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; not fixed (needs a schema change).

summary: A subscription outlives the right to hear it: owns is asked at open, a token's exp at the next request
detail: With auth, `owns` is asked when a socket opens a document and on each request, and jwtAuth's gate checks `exp` on each request; nothing checks either between requests. A socket taken off a document (owns now false) or whose token ran out keeps receiving every write through what it has open until it next asks for something. And when that request comes, jwtAuth drops the socket's subscriptions but leaves it connected, so the client's documents freeze with `connected` true and onConnect never runs again (the skill now says to re-authenticate and re-open on the 401). Repro: scratchpad/round2-delta-reviewer-2/pg-revoke.test.ts: Alice opens `items:`, is taken out of `owns`, Bob writes, and Alice's socket receives the add. Options: a `revoke(identity, docName)` / `dropIdentity` hook the app calls, owns re-asked per subscriber in drainDoc (a query per write per subscriber), and for expiry closing the socket (e.g. code 4401) so the reconnect runs onConnect with a fresh token.
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; design question.

summary: With auth, custom documents and hand-written DocTypes have no owns: any signed-in identity opens any name
detail: The default-deny in c4e39f7 lives in docTypeFromDef. A DocType registered by hand with no `owns` is never asked (the listener checks `found.type.owns` only when it is there), and a custom document (`defineCustomDoc`) has neither owns nor an identity in `parse`/`query`: a membership doc's query runs on the bare pool, its cache is shared across identities, and customFanOut publishes each matching row on the doc's channel. So with auth, any identity that passes the gate may open any custom doc name and hear every row it matches, RLS or not. Only `recompute` docs see the identity. From reading listener.ts (the open handler at 'if (customByPrefix.size > 0)' and customFanOut). Options: `owns` on CustomDocDef, and registerDocType refusing a DocType with no owns when the listener has auth (or a `shared` flag there too).
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; not fixed (API change).

summary: An onConnect that calls through DI (call("authenticate", params) with no client) deadlocks: the client never connects, and says nothing
detail: onConnect runs before `ready` resolves, and only the client it is given skips `ready`. `connectWs(url, { onConnect: () => call("authenticate", { token }) })` with `provide(WS, ...)` sends through inject(WS), which waits for `ready`, which waits for onConnect: `connected` stays false for good, no document opens, and nothing is logged. The docs show the right form (`(ws) => call(..., ws)`), but it is one missing argument. Repro: scratchpad/round2-delta-reviewer-2/onconnect-di.ts (HANG, connected: false). Options: a log.warn when onConnect has not settled after a few seconds, or a request made from inside onConnect's async context going straight out.
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; not fixed.

summary: SQLite applies a batch's field writes after its adds and removes, so a batch that changes a row and then removes it is a 404
detail: applyOps in sqlite.ts collects field replaces (and whole-row replaces) into rowFieldBatches and writes them after the loop over adds and removes. `[replace /items/y/name, remove /items/y]` fails 'Row not found: items/y' (the JSON file and Postgres apply it in order), and a batch's ops are not applied in the order sent. Found writing the net-change walk test (222f3ae): the SQLite case uses remove-then-add instead. Either apply in order, or say in the skill's side-by-side table that a SQLite batch writes fields last.
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; low.

summary: planWalk and _delta_walk_plan are one rule in two languages with no shared cases
detail: CLAUDE.md says to change them together, but nothing pins them together the way tests/postgres-pointer.test.ts pins the two pointer parsers: each backend has its own 'undo beside someone else' tests, written against its own schema. Round 2's review found both planned an entry that touched a row twice op by op (fixed in 222f3ae, in both); the next drift may be in one only. A list of { entry: { ops, inverse }, current, expected: { ops, conflict } } run through planWalk and through `SELECT _delta_walk_plan(...)` (with a stub delta_open, or a doc built for it) would. Belongs with todo #15's shared vectors.
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review.

file: (no repo home; proposed as a marketplace plugin)
summary: No shared blueshed plugin or router skill tells an agent which of eta, delta and railroad to use, and delta-doc's own description captures every 'live multi-user app' request before railroad or eta are considered
detail: architect.md §5: delta-doc's SKILL.md claims every 'live multi-user app' request (its description names greenfield apps choosing between Firebase, Supabase and the rest, and the body says 'the answer is delta-doc') and never mentions eta or railroad by name as an alternative; eta-app only fires inside the eta repo, so a greenfield 'build me a live app' request never reaches it even though eta's own README pitches exactly that. Proposed shape (architect §6.2, proposal-final §5): one `blueshed` plugin in a marketplace repo holding a router skill under about 800 words (the decision guide: different people see different slices of the same data, undo matters, forms and lists, one box -> eta; interaction-heavy UI, several processes, Postgres/RLS, other clients consuming the doc JSON -> delta + railroad; one very interactive widget inside eta -> an applet, optionally a railroad island; reactive UI with no sync -> railroad alone), plus WIRE.md, one sandbox hook, one release command and MCP wiring; package skills stay inside the npm packages, synced at session start, restricted to @blueshed/* plus an allowlist (delta's install-skills does this since 02b1926), and delta-doc's own description narrows to projects that have already chosen delta. Namespacing under `blueshed:` ends skill/command shadowing in multi-repo sessions (architect F2, now largely moot since delta re-syncs its vendored railroad skills at each railroad release) and retires each repo's own /publish once `release` lands. Same item in railroad's, delta's and eta's todo.jsonl.
note: 2026-09-24: from the review team's round 1; open, for Peter.

file: (.claude/hooks/session-start.sh: railroad's and delta's; eta has none)
summary: No Bun-only SessionStart hook serves railroad, delta and eta: railroad's and delta's upgrade Bun with npm, and eta has none
detail: railroad's hook upgrades Bun with npm, runs `npx playwright install-deps`, decompresses Chromium with `node -e`, lets each of those print to stdout, and under `set -u` aborts when CLAUDE_ENV_FILE is unset; delta's logs to stderr and guards the env file, but installs Bun with `npm install -g bun` on every start, which moves the container's Bun to the latest release whatever the project pins, and it stages no browser; eta has no hook, so nothing provisions the Chromium its Bun.WebView tests need (eta's todo #18) and a fresh eta web session cannot go green without another repo's setup by hand. Each repo's CLAUDE.md says Bun only. round2/eta.md §6 Proposal 6, architect.md F8 and §6.4: one Bun-only hook shared by the three (bunx, bun -e; progress to stderr; a guarded env file) that detects what the project needs (the Bun floor from engines.bun, Chromium if a test file uses Bun.WebView, Postgres if pg is a dependency, with the DELTA_TEST_PG_URL convention delta documents) instead of hard-coding it. Same item in railroad's, delta's and eta's todo.jsonl.
